name: Equisetaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach horsetails as true ferns with jointed hollow ribbed stems, whorled leaf sheaths, terminal strobili of peltate sporangiophores, and homosporous green spores with four hygroscopic elaters; reconcile the North American scouring-rush source to current Equisetum praealtum.

project_scope.selection_mode: Source Equisetum hyemale reconciled to current North American Equisetum praealtum
project_scope.note: The project source is Hays/Personal and therefore represents the North American scouring-rush concept historically treated as E. hyemale subsp. affine. Current Kew accepts that lineage as Equisetum praealtum; E. hyemale sensu stricto is Eurasian/SE Greenland.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at a stem node. The aerial stem is hollow, longitudinally ribbed and visibly jointed; tiny leaves are fused into a toothed sheath encircling each node.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Rhizomatous perennial herbs with silica-rich, cylindrical, hollow, ridged stems. Branches, when present, arise from nodes. Leaves are reduced microphylls in whorls and fused basally into a nodal sheath.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: A terminal cone-like strobilus is built from many peltate, umbrella-shaped sporangiophores; several sporangia hang from the underside of each sporangiophore.
family_diagnostics.spores: Homosporous. Spores are green/chlorophyllous and bear four hygroscopic elaters that coil and uncoil with humidity.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Jointed ribbed hollow stem + toothed sheath at every node + terminal strobilus = Equisetaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: jointed stem → nodal sheath → hollow/ridged cross-section → terminal strobilus → peltate sporangiophore → elater-bearing spore → praealtum taxonomy card → Joey Adiantum comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Horsetails look nothing like a typical fern, but they are part of the true-fern/monilophyte lineage. Their leaves are reduced to sheaths and the sporangia move into a terminal cone.

steps.title: 1 · Start at the joint
steps.look_for: Obvious nodes separating long ribbed internodes; dark or contrasting bands may accent the sheath.
steps.why_it_matters: The jointed architecture is the fastest family-level cue.

steps.title: 2 · Unwrap the leaf concept
steps.look_for: Many tiny scale leaves fused into a crown-like sheath with individual teeth at the rim.
steps.why_it_matters: Explains where the 'leaves' went and prevents treating the sheath as bark.

steps.title: 3 · Show the hollow ribbed stem
steps.look_for: Large central hollow cavity plus longitudinal ridges around the circumference.
steps.why_it_matters: Reinforces the structural basis of the scouring-rush silhouette.

steps.title: 4 · Open the strobilus architecture
steps.look_for: Terminal cone composed of shieldlike/peltate sporangiophores, each bearing multiple sporangia underneath.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the reproductive structure that replaces ordinary fern sori.

steps.title: 5 · Watch an elater-bearing spore
steps.look_for: A green spherical spore with four ribbonlike hygroscopic elaters.
steps.why_it_matters: A uniquely memorable Equisetum reproductive character.

steps.title: 6 · Fix the North American name
steps.look_for: Project source 'Equisetum hyemale' / older E. hyemale subsp. affine → current Equisetum praealtum for the North American lineage.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents the learner from assigning the Eurasian E. hyemale sensu stricto to a Texas plant.

steps.title: 7 · Compare with Joey's Adiantum
steps.look_for: Adiantum bears sporangia along the blade margin beneath a rolled pseudoindusium; Equisetum concentrates sporangia in a terminal strobilus on peltate sporangiophores.
steps.why_it_matters: Makes the huge body-plan diversity within true ferns visually concrete.

comparisons.title: Equisetaceae vs Selaginellaceae
comparisons.rule: Equisetaceae has hollow ribbed jointed stems, whorled fused leaf sheaths and homosporous terminal strobili. Selaginellaceae has leafy branching shoots with individual ligulate microphylls, rhizophores, and two spore sizes.

comparisons.title: Equisetaceae vs ordinary true ferns
comparisons.rule: Both are monilophytes, but Equisetum has reduced nodal leaves and terminal strobili; familiar ferns such as Adiantum carry sporangia in sori on a leafy frond.

comparisons.title: Equisetum praealtum naming
comparisons.rule: Older North American floras often call it E. hyemale subsp. affine. Current Kew treats that North American lineage as E. praealtum; E. hyemale sensu stricto is Eurasian/SE Greenland.

visual_lesson.caveat: The source pool currently says Equisetum hyemale, but a Texas/Hays scouring-rush should not be taught as Eurasian E. hyemale sensu stricto under the current Kew backbone. Species-level confirmation still belongs to the species lane.

genera.fast_cue: jointed hollow ridged stems + toothed nodal sheaths + terminal strobilus

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Project source is North American/Texas. Current Kew treats the North American E. hyemale subsp. affine / var. affine concept as E. praealtum.
Current Kew synonym; older FNA morphology remains useful.

taxonomy_reconciliation.name: Equisetum hyemale
taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Still an accepted species, but current Kew native range is SE Greenland and temperate Eurasia rather than Texas.
